questions.question: f(x) = 1/2 |kx - 9| - 2 for all real x, where k is a positive constant. (The modulus bars are not clear on the scan; the V-shaped graph and part (b) confirm this reading.) The graph cuts the y-axis at A and has a minimum point at B. (i) Find the y coordinate of A. (ii) Find, in terms of k, the x coordinate of B.
steps: So A has y coordinate 5/2 (2.5).
A modulus graph has its minimum where the inside is zero: kx - 9 = 0.
So B has x coordinate 9/k (its y coordinate is -2).

questions.question: For f(x) = 1/2 |kx - 9| - 2 as in part (a), find, in terms of k, the range of values of x that satisfy the inequality |kx - 9| - 2 < 0.
steps: Rewrite the inequality as |kx - 9| < 2.
Divide by k, which is positive: 7/k < x < 11/k.

questions.question: The line y = 3 - 2x intersects the graph y = f(x), where f(x) = 1/2 |kx - 9| - 2, at two distinct points. Find the range of possible values of k.
steps: Case kx >= 9: kx - 9 = 10 - 4x gives x = 19/(k + 4), valid when kx >= 9 (true for k >= 3.6).
Case kx < 9: 9 - kx = 10 - 4x gives x = 1/(4 - k), valid when kx < 9.
For k > 4 both cases give one valid root, so there are two distinct points.
For k <= 4 at most one root is valid (for example k = 3 gives x = 1 only).
So the range is k > 4.

questions.question: The point P(-4, -3) lies on the curve y = f(x). Find the point to which P is mapped when the curve is transformed to y = f(2x).
steps: For y = f(2x), a point (x0, y0) on y = f(x) maps to (x0/2, y0).
x0 = -4 gives x = -2.
The y coordinate is unchanged at -3.

questions.question: The point P(-4, -3) lies on the curve y = f(x). Find the point to which P is mapped when the curve is transformed to y = 3f(x - 1).
steps: For y = 3f(x - 1), a point (x0, y0) on y = f(x) maps to (x0 + 1, 3y0).

questions.question: The point P(-4, -3) lies on the curve y = f(x). Find the point to which P is mapped when the curve is transformed to y = |f(x)|.
steps: The x coordinate is unchanged.
The y coordinate becomes |-3| = 3.
Any part below the x axis is reflected above it.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows the graph of y = a - |2x - b| where a and b are positive constants with a > b. Find, in terms of a and b: (i) the coordinates of the maximum point; (ii) the coordinates of the point where the graph meets the y axis; (iii) the coordinates of the points where the graph meets the x axis. (Parts (i) to (iii) share one mark allocation of 5.)
questions.answer: (i) maximum (b/2, a); (ii) (0, a - b); (iii) ((b - a)/2, 0) and ((a + b)/2, 0)
steps: The maximum occurs when |2x - b| = 0, so x = b/2 and y = a: maximum (b/2, a).
Put x = 0: y = a - |-b| = a - b, giving (0, a - b).
Put y = 0: |2x - b| = a, so 2x - b = a or 2x - b = -a.
Since a > b, (b - a)/2 is negative, which matches the figure.

questions.question: On Diagram 1, sketch the graph with equation y = |x| - 1, showing the vertex and the points where it meets the axes.
questions.answer: V shape with vertex (0, -1), crossing the x axis at (-1, 0) and (1, 0), and the y axis at (0, -1)
steps: For x >= 0 the graph is y = x - 1; for x < 0 it is y = -x - 1.
The vertex is the minimum point (0, -1).
It crosses the x axis where |x| = 1, so at (-1, 0) and (1, 0).
Draw both branches rising away from the vertex with gradients -1 and 1.

questions.question: The graphs y = |x| - 1 and y = a - |2x - b| intersect at x = -3 and x = 5. Given that a and b are positive constants with a > b, find the value of a and the value of b.
steps: So a - b = 8.
Solving a - b = 8 and a + b = 14 gives a = 11, b = 3.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a sketch of y = |3x - 5a| - 2a, where a is a positive constant. The graph cuts the y axis at P, cuts the x axis at Q and R (Q to the left of R) and has a minimum point at S. Find, in simplest form in terms of a, the coordinates of P, of Q and R, and of S. (Parts (i) to (iii) share one mark allocation of 4.)
steps: P: put x = 0, giving |-5a| - 2a = 3a, so P = (0, 3a).
Q and R: |3x - 5a| = 2a, so 3x - 5a = 2a or 3x - 5a = -2a.
3x = 7a gives R = (7a/3, 0); 3x = 3a gives Q = (a, 0).
S: the minimum is where 3x - 5a = 0, so x = 5a/3 and y = -2a.

questions.question: Find, in simplest form in terms of a, the values of x for which |3x - 5a| - 2a = |x - 2a|, where a is a positive constant.
steps: Critical points are x = 5a/3 and x = 2a, with 5a/3 < 2a.
Region x < 5a/3: 5a - 3x - 2a = 2a - x gives x = a/2, which is valid.
Region 5a/3 <= x < 2a: 3x - 7a = 2a - x gives x = 9a/4, which is outside the region.
Region x >= 2a: 3x - 7a = x - 2a gives x = 5a/2, which is valid.
Check x = a/2: both sides equal 3a/2.

questions.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = 2x^2 - 5, x >= 0, x real. State the range of f.
steps: f is increasing for x >= 0.
f(0) = -5 is the smallest value.
So the range is f(x) >= -5.

questions.question: Diagram 1 shows a sketch of y = f(x) where f(x) = 2x^2 - 5, x >= 0. On Diagram 1, sketch the curve with equation y = f^-1(x).
questions.answer: Reflection of y = f(x) in y = x: starts at (-5, 0), rises to the right through (0, sqrt(2.5)) approx (0, 1.58)
steps: Find f^-1: y + 5 = 2x^2, so x = sqrt((y + 5)/2), giving f^-1(x) = sqrt((x + 5)/2) for x >= -5.
Reflect the curve y = f(x) in the line y = x.
The point (0, -5) on f maps to (-5, 0) on f^-1.
f^-1 crosses the y axis at (0, sqrt(2.5)) approx (0, 1.58) and rises slowly to the right.

questions.question: The curve y = f(x) meets the curve y = f^-1(x) at the point P, where f(x) = 2x^2 - 5, x >= 0. Using algebra and showing working, find the exact x coordinate of P.
steps: Let P = (p, q). Then q = f(p) and f(q) = p, with p, q >= 0.
So 2p^2 - 5 = q and 2q^2 - 5 = p.
Subtracting: 2(p - q)(p + q) = q - p, so (p - q)(2p + 2q + 1) = 0.
Since 2p + 2q + 1 > 0, p = q.
Take the positive root: x = (1 + sqrt(41))/4 approx 1.851.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows y = f(x), a polynomial curve through the origin with a maximum turning point at (1, 2) and a minimum turning point at (3, 0). On a separate diagram, sketch y = 3f(2x), showing the point where the curve crosses the y axis and any maximum or minimum turning points.
questions.answer: Crosses y axis at (0, 0); maximum (0.5, 6); minimum (1.5, 0)
steps: y = 3f(2x) stretches the graph parallel to the x axis by factor 1/2 and parallel to the y axis by factor 3.
Map each point (x, y) on y = f(x) to (x/2, 3y).
(1, 2) maps to (0.5, 6), the maximum.
(3, 0) maps to (1.5, 0), the minimum.

questions.question: Using the curve y = f(x) from Figure 1 (passing through the origin, maximum at (1, 2), minimum at (3, 0)), sketch y = f(-x) - 1, showing the point where the curve crosses the y axis and any maximum or minimum turning points.
questions.answer: Crosses y axis at (0, -1); maximum (-1, 1); minimum (-3, -1)
steps: Reflect in the y axis: (x, y) maps to (-x, y).
Translate down 1: (x, y) maps to (-x, y - 1).
(0, 0) maps to (0, -1), the y intercept.
(1, 2) maps to (-1, 1), the maximum.
(3, 0) maps to (-3, -1), the minimum.

questions.question: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = (4x + 6)/(x - 5), x real, x != 5, and g(x) = 5 - 2x^2, x real, x <= 0. Solve the equation fg(x) = 3.
steps: fg(x) = f(g(x)). Let y = g(x) = 5 - 2x^2.
Since x <= 0, x = -sqrt(13).

questions.question: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = (4x + 6)/(x - 5), x real, x != 5, and g(x) = 5 - 2x^2, x <= 0. Find f^-1.
steps: Expand: xy - 5y = 4x + 6.
Collect x: x(y - 4) = 5y + 6.
Swap x and y: f^-1(x) = (5x + 6)/(x - 4).

questions.question: The functions g(x) = 5 - 2x^2 (x <= 0) and f are as above. Sketch and label, on the same axes, the curve y = g(x) and the curve y = g^-1(x). On your sketch show the coordinates of the points where each curve meets or cuts the coordinate axes.
questions.answer: g: (0, 5) and (-sqrt(2.5), 0); g^-1: (5, 0) and (0, -sqrt(2.5)); the curves meet at ((-1 - sqrt(41))/4, same) approx (-1.851, -1.851)
steps: g(x) = 5 - 2x^2 for x <= 0: maximum at (0, 5), decreasing as x goes to -infinity.
It crosses the x axis at x = -sqrt(2.5) approx -1.58.
g^-1(x) = -sqrt((5 - x)/2) for x <= 5 is the reflection of g in y = x.
g^-1 crosses the x axis at (5, 0) and the y axis at (0, -sqrt(2.5)).
The curves meet on y = x: 2x^2 + x - 5 = 0, and with x <= 0 this gives x = (-1 - sqrt(41))/4 approx -1.85.

questions.question: Figure 3 shows a sketch of the graph C1 with equation y = 5 - |3x - 22|. (i) Write down the coordinates of the vertex of C1. (ii) Write down the coordinates of the intersection of C1 with the y axis. (Parts (i) and (ii) share one mark allocation of 2.)
steps: The vertex is where 3x - 22 = 0, so x = 22/3 and y = 5.
So the y intercept is (0, -17).

questions.question: The graph C1 has equation y = 5 - |3x - 22|. Find the x coordinates of the intersections of C1 with the x axis.
steps: 3x - 22 = 5 gives x = 9.

questions.question: Diagram 1 is a copy of Figure 3, which shows C1 with equation y = 5 - |3x - 22|. On Diagram 1, sketch the curve C2 with equation y = x^2/9 - 9. Identify clearly the coordinates of any points of intersection of C2 with the coordinate axes.
questions.answer: C2 is a parabola with minimum (0, -9); meets y axis at (0, -9) and x axis at (-9, 0) and (9, 0)
steps: y = x^2/9 - 9 is a parabola opening upwards with minimum point (0, -9).
Put y = 0: x^2 = 81, so x = -9 or x = 9.
Points on the x axis: (-9, 0) and (9, 0).

questions.question: Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of C1 with equation y = 5 - |3x - 22| and C2 with equation y = x^2/9 - 9. Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.
steps: Only x = 9 is valid (x >= 22/3); then y = 81/9 - 9 = 0, giving (9, 0).
Only x = 3 is valid (x < 22/3); then y = 9/9 - 9 = -8, giving (3, -8).

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a sketch of the curve y = |2 - 4ln(x + 1)| for x > k, where k is a constant. The curve has an asymptote at x = k, cuts the y axis at A and meets the x axis at B. State the value of k.
steps: The modulus grows without bound when ln(x + 1) tends to -infinity.
This happens when x + 1 tends to 0, so x tends to -1.
So the asymptote is x = -1 and k = -1.

questions.question: The curve y = |2 - 4ln(x + 1)| meets the y axis at A and the x axis at B, as in Figure 2. (i) Find the y coordinate of A. (ii) Find the exact x coordinate of B. (Parts (i) and (ii) share one mark allocation of 3.)
questions.answer: (i) A = (0, 2), so y = 2; (ii) B has x = sqrt(e) - 1
steps: (ii) B is where 2 - 4ln(x + 1) = 0, so ln(x + 1) = 1/2.

questions.question: Using algebra and showing your working, find the set of values of x such that |2 - 4ln(x + 1)| > 3, for x > -1.
steps: Let u = ln(x + 1). We need |2 - 4u| > 3.
Either 2 - 4u > 3, giving u < -1/4.
Or 2 - 4u < -3, giving u > 5/4.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows a sketch of part of y = f(x) where f(x) = 2|3 - x| + 5, x >= 0. Solve the equation f(x) = (1/2)x + 30.
steps: Case 0 <= x <= 3: 2(3 - x) + 5 = x/2 + 30 gives 11 - 2x = x/2 + 30, so x = -7.6, which is not valid.
x = 62/3, which is greater than 3, so it is valid.

questions.question: f(x) = 2|3 - x| + 5, x >= 0, as in Figure 1. Given that f(x) = k, where k is a constant, has two distinct roots, state the set of possible values for k.
steps: The minimum value of f is 5 at x = 3.
f(0) = 11, and f decreases from 11 to 5 on 0 <= x <= 3.
For 5 < k < 11 there are two roots, one on each side of x = 3.
At k = 11 the roots are x = 0 and x = 6, which are still two distinct roots.
For k > 11 there is only one root.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows part of the graph y = f(x) where f(x) = 2|2x - 5| + 3, x >= 0. The vertex of the graph is at P. State the coordinates of P.
steps: The vertex is where 2x - 5 = 0, so x = 5/2.

questions.question: The graph y = f(x) with f(x) = 2|2x - 5| + 3, x >= 0. Solve the equation f(x) = 3x - 2.
steps: 15/7 (approx 2.14) lies in [0, 2.5), so it is valid.
Check x = 5: both sides equal 13. Check x = 15/7: both sides equal 31/7.

questions.question: The graph y = f(x) with f(x) = 2|2x - 5| + 3, x >= 0. Given that the equation f(x) = kx + 2, where k is a constant, has exactly two roots, find the range of values of k.
steps: The left piece meets y = kx + 2 at x = 11/(4 + k), valid when x <= 5/2, i.e. k >= 2/5.
The right piece meets it at x = 9/(4 - k), valid when x >= 5/2 and k < 4.
At k = 2/5 both give x = 5/2, so the two roots coincide; we need k > 2/5.
For k >= 4 only the left root remains, so the range is 2/5 < k < 4.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a sketch of y = f(x) where f(x) = |3x + a| + a and a is a positive constant. The graph has a vertex at P. Find, in terms of a, the coordinates of P.
steps: The vertex is where 3x + a = 0, so x = -a/3.
Then f(-a/3) = 0 + a = a.

questions.question: Sketch the graph with equation y = g(x), where g(x) = |x + 5a| and a is a positive constant. On your sketch, show the coordinates, in terms of a, of each point where the graph cuts or meets the coordinate axes.
questions.answer: V shape with vertex (-5a, 0); crosses y axis at (0, 5a)
steps: The vertex is where x + 5a = 0, giving (-5a, 0).
Put x = 0: g(0) = |5a| = 5a, giving (0, 5a).
The graph has gradient -1 to the left of the vertex and +1 to the right.

questions.question: The graph with equation y = g(x), where g(x) = |x + 5a|, intersects the graph with equation y = f(x), where f(x) = |3x + a| + a, at two points. Find, in terms of a, the coordinates of the two points.
steps: Solve |x + 5a| = |3x + a| + a, with critical points x = -5a and x = -a/3.
For x >= -a/3: x + 5a = 3x + 2a gives x = 3a/2, which is valid.
For -5a <= x < -a/3: x + 5a = -3x gives x = -5a/4, which is valid.
For x < -5a: -x - 5a = -3x gives x = 5a/2, which is not valid.

questions.question: Given that k is a positive constant, on separate diagrams sketch (i) y = k - 2|x| and (ii) y = |2x - k/3|. Show on each sketch the coordinates, in terms of k, of each point where the graph meets or cuts the axes.
questions.answer: (i) maximum (0, k), x intercepts (-k/2, 0) and (k/2, 0); (ii) vertex (k/6, 0), y intercept (0, k/3)
steps: (i) Inverted V with maximum (0, k) and gradients -2 and 2 away from it.
Set y = 0: |x| = k/2, so x = -k/2 or x = k/2.
(ii) V shape with vertex where 2x - k/3 = 0, giving (k/6, 0).
Put x = 0: y = |-k/3| = k/3, giving (0, k/3).

questions.question: Given that k is a positive constant, hence find, in terms of k, the values of x for which |2x - k/3| = k - 2|x|, giving your answers in simplest form.
steps: The right side must be non-negative, so |x| <= k/2.
Case x >= k/6: 2x - k/3 = k - 2x gives x = k/3, which is valid.
Case 0 <= x < k/6: k/3 - 2x = k - 2x gives k/3 = k, which is impossible.
Case x < 0: k/3 - 2x = k + 2x gives x = -k/6, which is valid.
Check x = k/3: both sides equal k/3. Check x = -k/6: both sides equal 2k/3.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows part of the graph y = f(x) where f(x) = (1/2)|2x + 7| - 10. The graph has a vertex V. State the coordinates of V.
steps: The vertex is where 2x + 7 = 0, so x = -7/2.

questions.question: The graph y = f(x) with f(x) = (1/2)|2x + 7| - 10. Using algebra, solve (1/2)|2x + 7| - 10 >= (1/3)x + 1.
steps: Since (1/2)|2x + 7| = |x + 7/2|, the inequality becomes |x + 7/2| >= x/3 + 11.
Case x >= -7/2: x + 7/2 >= x/3 + 11 gives x >= 45/4, which is valid.
Case x < -7/2: -(x + 7/2) >= x/3 + 11 gives x <= -87/8, which is valid.
Check x = 45/4: both sides equal 4.75. Check x = -87/8: both sides equal -2.625.

questions.question: For f(x) = (1/2)|2x + 7| - 10, sketch the graph with equation y = |f(x)|, stating the coordinates of the local maximum point and each local minimum point.
questions.answer: Local maximum (-7/2, 10); local minima at (-27/2, 0) and (13/2, 0)
steps: f is below the x axis between these points, so |f| reflects that part upwards.
The vertex (-7/2, -10) becomes (-7/2, 10), a local maximum.
The points (-27/2, 0) and (13/2, 0) become local minima on the x axis.
Also f(0) = -13/2, so |f(0)| = 6.5 gives the y intercept (0, 6.5).

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a sketch of y = f(x) where f(x) = 3|x - 2| - 10. The vertex of the graph is at point P. Find the coordinates of P.
steps: The vertex is where x - 2 = 0, so x = 2.

questions.question: For f(x) = 3|x - 2| - 10, find ff(0).
steps: So ff(0) = 8.

questions.question: Solve the inequality 3|x - 2| - 10 < 5x + 10 for f(x) = 3|x - 2| - 10.
steps: Rewrite as 3|x - 2| < 5x + 20.
For x >= 2: 3x - 6 < 5x + 20 holds for all x >= 2.
For x < 2: 6 - 3x < 5x + 20 gives x > -7/4.
Combining the two cases gives x > -7/4.

questions.question: For f(x) = 3|x - 2| - 10, solve the equation f(|x|) = 0.
steps: |x| - 2 = -10/3 gives |x| = -4/3, which has no solution.

questions.question: Figure 1 shows a sketch of part of y = f(x) where f(x) = |3x - 13| + 5, x real. The vertex of the graph is at point P. State the coordinates of P.
steps: The vertex is where 3x - 13 = 0, so x = 13/3.

questions.question: For f(x) = |3x - 13| + 5, x real: (i) state the range of f; (ii) find the value of ff(4).
Solve, using algebra and showing working, the inequality 16 - 2x > |3x - 13| + 5.
steps: Rewrite as |3x - 13| < 11 - 2x, which needs 11 - 2x > 0, so x < 11/2.
Case x < 13/3: 13 - 3x < 11 - 2x gives x > 2.
Combining both cases gives 2 < x < 24/5.
Check x = 3: 10 > 9, which holds.

questions.question: The graph y = f(x), where f(x) = |3x - 13| + 5, is transformed onto the graph y = af(x + b). The vertex of y = af(x + b) is (4, 20). Given that a and b are constants, find the value of a and the value of b.
steps: The vertex of y = f(x) is (13/3, 5).
For y = af(x + b), the vertex is where x + b = 13/3, so x = 13/3 - b.
The y value at the vertex is a x 5 = 20, so a = 4.

questions.question: Figure 2 shows a sketch of part of y = f(x) where f(x) = 21 - 2|2 - x|, x >= 0. Find ff(6).
For f(x) = 21 - 2|2 - x|, x >= 0, solve the equation f(x) = 5x.
steps: Case x >= 2: 21 - 2(x - 2) = 5x gives 25 = 7x, so x = 25/7, which is valid.
Case 0 <= x < 2: 21 - 2(2 - x) = 5x gives 3x = 17, so x = 17/3, which is not in the range.

questions.question: For f(x) = 21 - 2|2 - x|, x >= 0, the equation f(x) = k, where k is a constant, has exactly two roots. State the set of possible values of k.
steps: The maximum value is 21 at x = 2, and f(0) = 17.
On [0, 2] f increases from 17 to 21; on [2, infinity) f decreases from 21 towards -infinity.
For 17 < k < 21 there are two roots, one on each branch.
For k = 17 the roots are x = 0 and x = 4, which are two distinct roots.
For k = 21 or k < 17 there is only one root.

questions.question: The graph y = f(x), where f(x) = 21 - 2|2 - x|, is transformed onto the graph y = af(x - b). The vertex of the graph y = af(x - b) is (6, 3). Given that a and b are constants, find the value of a and the value of b.
steps: The vertex of y = f(x) is (2, 21).
The vertex of y = af(x - b) is (2 + b, 21a).
2 + b = 6 gives b = 4.
21a = 3 gives a = 1/7.
